title: George Lewis, Manny's Tavern and Millenburg
summary: Interviewer asks about places where George Lewis played, Silver City, Boscoville and Millenburg.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah. That's where, uh, uh, George Lewis used to play back there, how you call it?
Sure, George Lewis, oh, George Lewis played all around in that. I guess even before I was born.

Manny's was back there, Manny's Tavern. That was in Lover's Land? Yeah, Manny's Tavern and Lover's Land. That's right. And how you call it, uh, uh, there was a restaurant back there, uh, to drive in, and I, Wallace and Raoul's was right over the Elver Pass. You remember Wallace and Raoul's?

It was a, uh, cement block building, and I think it, uh, I think a lot of people used to hang around there and make a drop or something. I don't know. Stuff like that. Anyway, and what about, uh, Silver City? Were you ever in Silver City?
Well, Boscoville, that's all back that way where I'm telling you about it, but Boscoville is behind those little places. It's the last thing, uh, the last thing close to the lake.
Yeah, it's way back on the other side Gentilly.
Now what about Millenburg? How far is it from Millenburg?

Well, Millenburg, well, Millenburg is like, you see, you may as well say that's by the lake, that Millenburg. You see? Now they got another place back that way, but on the other side, like Franklin Avenue, but way back. Uh-huh. I mean, Placiatum live right now. Uh, they call it the Seabrooks, but you never hardly hear people say anything about Seabrooks. No, not much anymore. Not much anymore.
That's the bridge, there's a bridge.
They named the bridge that, though, Seabrook Bridge.
Yeah, they do say that, Gentilly.
